I notice some inconsistency when naming this basic theorem. We have

  • docs#Nat.dvd_iff_mod_eq_zero
  • docs#Int.dvd_iff_mod_eq_zero
  • docs#Ordinal.dvd_iff_mod_eq_zero

And yet, the version for EuclideanDomain is called

  • docs#EuclideanDomain.mod_eq_zero

Would it be desirable to rename (and flip the direction) of this last one to match the others?

(The second link you posted gives 404)
The last one for EuclideanDomain is tagged with @[simp], while all ohters in loogle are not.
Since a | b is arguably simples that a % b = 0 I would say the simp is in the correct direction.

So maybe it would even be reasonable to flip the other ones and tag them with simp?
Hmm, not sure about that for nat/int, if the values are explicit numbers, % is an explicit calculation and | is an existence claim
